unit.content: Budget; Discounts, and commission; Profit and loss; Conversion of different currencies
unit.coreCompetencies:
Citizenship: The learner develops ethical and digital citizenship skills when obtaining digital or printed currency exchange rates charts/tables, and working out currency conversion from Kenya Shillings to any other currencies.
Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner acquires interpretation and inference skills when role play shopping scenarios where discounts are given and work out the discounts and the percentage discount.
unit.values:
Peace: the learner respects self and others by listening to others’ opinion while brainstorming brainstorm scenarios under which commissions are paid to salespersons for sale of goods and services.
Patriotism: the learner displays loyalty by showing love for one's own country's currency when obtaining digital or printed currency exchange rates tables and working out currency conversion from Kenya Shillings to any other currencies.
unit.pcis: Financial literacy: the learner’s financial skills are enhanced when obtaining digital or printed currency exchange rates charts/tables, and working out currency conversion from Kenya Shillings to any other currencies.
unit.sep: Mathematical modelling, proportional reasoning and verification.
unit.careers: Bookkeeping, retail, sales and financial administration.
unit.focus: Prepare, calculate and justify everyday financial decisions with explicit percentage bases and exchange-rate direction.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional school club can balance its first budget but wants to know whether advertised discounts and exchange offers improve its position.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Illustrative quotations, sales agreements and a dealer exchange board. Figures are not real market prices or current rates.
unit.drivingQuestion: How can a school club make and defend an affordable financial decision? KICD: Why do we need a budget? Why are discounts and commissions necessary in trading activities?
unit.storylineThread: Budget -> discounts -> commission -> profit/loss -> currency direction -> reverse conversion -> integrated decision -> communication -> independent assessment.

assessment.instructions: Time: 30 minutes within Lesson 9. Work independently using E9. A basic calculator is allowed. Show the percentage base and currency direction. Round final monetary amounts to 2 decimal places where needed. All data are illustrative; no taxes or additional fees apply.

sections.title: 1. Budget and discount
sections.prompt: Use E9. Calculate the discounted cost of 20 books, total planned allocation including transport and reserve, and unallocated funds. Explain why the reserve is included.
sections.exemplar: Discount per book=120×0.15=18 KES; net 102 KES.20 books=2040 KES. Total=2040+500+300=2840 KES. Unallocated=4000−2840=1160 KES. Reserve is planned money held for contingencies, so it is already part of the allocation.

sections.title: 2. Commission
sections.prompt: Calculate the salesperson’s commission in E9. State the base used.
sections.exemplar: 3% of 8000 KES=240 KES; base is total sales of 8000 KES.

sections.title: 3. Percentage profit
sections.prompt: Calculate the stall’s profit and its percentage profit on cost.

sections.title: 4. Currency directions
sections.prompt: Using E9, calculate(a) KES received when selling USD 20 to the dealer and(b) KES needed to buy USD 20. Explain which rate applies in each case.
sections.exemplar: (a) Dealer buys USD: 20×125=2500 KES.(b) Dealer sells USD: 20×130=2600 KES. The labels describe the dealer’s actions.

sections.title: 5. Explain a decision
sections.prompt: State one practical benefit of preparing a budget and one detail you would check before accepting a real quotation or exchange offer.
sections.exemplar: A budget tests affordability and allocates limited funds. Check an applicable detail such as quantity, marked price, fees, date or the dealer’s buying/selling direction. Accept another justified practical example.
